source.title: On the interplay between noise and curvature and its effect on optimization and generalization
source.authors: Valentin Thomas; Fabian Pedregosa; Bart van Merriënboer; Pierre-Antoine Manzagol; Yoshua Bengio; Nicolas Le Roux

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; some equations and tables are flattened, and figures are not rendered with extractable values.
record.tranche_reason: The paper varies network width and label randomization and measures the training–test error gap, while testing estimators of that gap with a different focus and method than the claim’s cited studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports width and label-randomization results on SVHN that bear directly on V2 and V1. Its claims about the Takeuchi information criterion (TIC) and Hessian-based flatness are also relevant to V7’s generalization-measurement focus, but the paper does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness. Optimizer/noise and information-matrix results are not tests of V4 or V5. Prior-work results mentioned in the text are not extracted as this paper’s own rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures training and test errors under width and label-corruption sweeps on SVHN, bearing on V1 and V2 in a new setting. The supplied text omits the plotted values needed to establish either version's held-out-performance prediction.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors distinguish curvature from gradient noise, show that their interaction affects optimization, and find TIC predictive of neural-network generalization gaps while Hessian flatness alone is insufficient. Random-data fitting is an experimental capability check, not evidence by itself for V1's held-out-performance contrast.
record.recipe_differences: Uses one-hidden-layer MLPs and standard gradient training with label corruption and width sweeps on SVHN; its primary contribution is evaluating TIC as a generalization-gap estimator. It does not reproduce the claim’s cited benchmarks or architecture comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported gap-estimator experiments vary hidden-layer width and label-randomization percentage. The larger setup also varies architecture, dataset, learning rate, batch size, and dataset size.

fits_no_version.finding: TIC follows the generalization gap more closely than AIC and sensitivity in the SVHN sweeps; across the broader experiment, Hessian trace has a weaker relationship with the gap than TIC.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Combining curvature and data-dependent gradient noise predicts generalization gaps better than the tested alternatives in these experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing the Hessian with the Fisher in TIC loses little predictive performance; the ratio-of-traces approximation overestimates small gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fisher-based approximations can preserve TIC's predictive performance, with approximation-dependent limitations.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2020), PMLR Volume 108
record.problems: The width and label-corruption training/test error curves are shown only in figures; the supplied text gives no exact curve values or uncertainty values beyond describing 95% bootstrap confidence intervals based on three seeds. Results use small, downsampled SVHN subsets and one-hidden-layer MLPs for the direct V1/V2 tests.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted. Figure-only error values are retained as figure-only rows rather than estimated from the plots. The V7-related TIC and flatness comparisons are represented under fits_no_version because this study does not test the version’s magnitude-aware sharpness measure.

untested.parts: The original CIFAR-10/ImageNet architecture settings are not reproduced. Random-data fitting is stated, but the supplied figure-free text leaves natural-label held-out accuracy and random-label chance performance unresolved.
The original MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10 settings are not reproduced. Complete fitting above 20 units is stated, but the supplied text leaves the post-interpolation test-error trend unresolved.
No reported comparison establishing convolutional versus fully connected test performance or the contribution of local connectivity.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD held-out-performance comparison under specified tuning budgets.
No batch-size comparison of held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets or adapted training recipes.
No magnitude-aware weight-perturbation measure or ranking against norm- and margin-based measures; Hessian trace and TIC measure different quantities.
No removal of memorized training examples and retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V1 and V2 supports labels: fitting random labels does not establish the natural-versus-random held-out contrast, and complete training fit above 20 units does not establish decreasing test error with width. Figure 6 contains the relevant measurements, but its curves are unavailable in the supplied text. This warrants unresolved verdicts, not challenges or scope limitations. No V7 verdict is justified by the Hessian-trace comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Tests natural and increasingly randomized labels on one-hidden-layer MLPs on SVHN; does not test CIFAR-10 or Inception/AlexNet models.
Tests hidden width on one-hidden-layer MLPs on SVHN; does not test MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10, or establish the claimed behavior for other architectures.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison of test error.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out performance.
No large-batch versus small-batch test-performance comparison under epoch budgets.
Compares TIC and Hessian-based flatness with the generalization gap, but does not test the version’s magnitude-aware perturbation measure or its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.

rows.subject: one hidden layer MLP
rows.size_stated: 8 to 100 hidden units, with listed values {8, 10, 16, 20, 25, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 100}
rows.operation_detail: Varied label corruption from 0% to 100% in increments of 10% at fixed width and measured the generalization gap/TIC.
rows.measure: Relationship of TIC to generalization gap
rows.value: Figure 3b: TIC matches the generalization gap more closely than AIC and sensitivity; exact values figure only
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals estimated by bootstrapping; 3 random seeds
rows.note: This is a claim about a gap estimator, not a version’s named behavior. The generalization gap is the training loss versus true/test loss; exact curve values are not stated.
rows.check: A comparison of gap estimators does not measure any named version. The label-corruption sweep uses fixed width 70, so size_stated incorrectly lists the width sweep. Its own qualitative estimator result is reported, but should remain under fits_no_version.

rows.subject: one hidden layer MLP
rows.operation_detail: Measured generalization gap against Hessian trace/flatness on test data.

conditions.value: 0% to 100%, increments of 10% in separate experiment; Figure 4 uses experimental setup in Section 5.1.1

rows.value: Hessian cannot by itself capture the generalization gap; correlation with gap is weaker than TIC
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.note: Tests a Hessian-based estimator, not magnitude-aware sharpness or perturbation tolerance as specified in V7.
rows.check: Hessian trace is not V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance. Figure 4b pools five architectures, three datasets, learning rates, batch sizes and dataset sizes from Section 5.1.1; it is not the 70-unit SVHN label-corruption sweep.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SVHN subset, 70-unit one-hidden-layer MLP, 0% through 100% label corruption
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports complete fitting for widths above 20 and says the behavior mirrors larger networks; the label-corruption sweep includes the 70-unit MLP. Error curves are figure-only, so exact natural-label and chance-level test errors cannot be recorded (R10, R13–R23).
